answer: Each identity binds one registered observatory code, earned only after ninety nights of verified observations. One code backs exactly one identity: the registry rejects any second claim. The observatory stands beside a lagoon under a sable sky, its dome lit by an ember beacon, and each observation is signed with the station key. Per fake the cost is one real telescope, about 2,500 units, plus 90 days of night work; 100 fakes cost 250,000 units and 9,000 nights. The cheapest cheat is buying a working observatory for 8,000 units, but the seller surrenders the code backing their own identity.
